answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a non-refundable bond and bind a unique hardware attestation from a trusted execution environment. Registration issues one credential per attested enclave, so an attacker cannot clone ten thousand agents from a single machine. Each fake persona costs real capital and distinct silicon, making mass duplication as expensive as trekking a ridge, a dune, and a canyon. When a sybil is detected, its bond is slashed and redistributed to honest peers, so impersonation loses money instead of earning it.
